question: Should OpenClaw adopt externalResolution as a permanent optional Gateway/plugin/Swift approval contract now, before the verifier runtime and provider-specific plugin implementation land?
rationale: The implementation is intentionally behavior-neutral, but public plugin and protocol surface choices are expensive to revise after external clients adopt them; code review cannot determine whether maintainers want this contract frozen independently of the full runtime stack.

options.title: Approve the contract slice
options.body: Confirm the provider-neutral object and two decision literals as the intended public API, then land it after a current-main refresh.

options.title: Land only with a broader stack
options.body: Pause this PR until the durable host runtime and executable consumer slices are ready for one combined API decision.

options.title: Request an API revision
options.body: Keep the PR open while the approval owner narrows, renames, or otherwise revises the long-term plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the contract slice
recommendation.body: Confirm the provider-neutral object and two decision literals as the intended public API, then land it after a current-main refresh.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical tracker identifies Kevin as having accepted the RFC design, so this is the strongest available routing signal for the public-contract decision.
